Md Mansur Habib with Md Zainul Abedin, Advocates—For the Appellant. 
Md Abu Kaiser, Assistant Attorney-General—For the State.
parties:
Abdul Wahed alias Chandu Mia ------ Petitioner
VS
State ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md Tafazzal Islam J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 5-5-90 passed by the Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal Judge Rangpur in Special Tribunal Case No. 10 of 1990 convicting the appellant under section 316 of the Penal Code and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 5(five) years and also fine of Taka 2,000.00 only in default to suffer 6(six) months more.

2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that one Mosammat Monsefa Khatun, the Prosecutrix, filed a complaint petition on 25-8-88, which subsequently on 17-10-88 was treated as the First Information Report, stating, inter alia, that in the night following 18-8-1988 while the Prosecotrix was sleeping with her two other sisters PWs 2 and 3, in a room by the side of the room of her brother PW 4, the appellant entered into her room through a gap between the wall and the roof of the room and undressed her and started committing rape on her whereupon she woke up and shouted saying কে কে and at the time the appellant disclosed his identity and asked her to remain silent and then gagged her mouth with his hand and at that time at the sound of the scuffle PWs 2 and 3 woke up and they started shouting and then PW 2 brought out the match from below her pillow and after lighting the match stick kindled the kupi bati and saw the appellant fleeing away through the gap by climbing with the help of a rope he tied with the beam of the roof for descending, and the PW 2 then tried to catch hold the appellant by grabbing his leg but could not get hold of him and on hearing the shout of the prosecutrix and PWs 2 and 3 their father as well as many other persons from the neighbourhood came running and heard the incident from them. Thereafter the witnesses along with other villagers tried to get hold of the appellant but could not succeed as he absconded and then on 19-8-1988 and 20-8-1988 there were salish over this matter and due to the salish there was delay in filing the complaint. The police after investigation submitted charge sheet against the appellant under sections 376/511 Penal Code. The prosecution in total examined nine witnesses and the defence examined only one and out of the nine PWs only four i.e. PWs 1 to 4 are charge sheeted witnesses. The defence case is that, the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has long standing land dispute with the father of the informant.

3. PW I the Prosecotrix stated that there is a partition wall between her room and the adjacent room of their house and there is a gap between the partition wall and the roof and while she was sleeping someone tried to rape her after undressing her and when she shouted কে কে someone gagged her mouth with his hand and she then tried to protect herself and by the sound of the scuffle her sisters PW 2 and 3 woke up and PW 2 lighted kupi batti and the Prosecotrix then found the appellant has done this work and that the appellant had a torch in his hand, he was fleeing away from the room by climbing on the roof with the help of the rope he tied with the beam of the roof. She further stated that the appellant discharged semen inside her private parts and that after hearing hue and cry brother PW 4, uncle Asgar and some other people of the village came to the place of occurrence and she then narrated the incident to them and then the witnesses along with villagers went to the house of the appellant but could not find him in his house and on the next day there was a salish and she went to the salish but the appellant did not turn up in the salish and subsequently there was another salish in the Union Parishad Office where the Chairman and Member of Union Parishad were present but the appellant did not also turn up in the said salish and then she, according to the advice of the persons present in the salish, went to lodge an ejahar with the thana but the thana authority did not accept the case and she therefore, filed the complaint case in the court of the local upazila Magistrate. During cross-examination the Prosecotrix denied the suggestion of the defence that in the First Information Report she did not mention the name of PWs 5, 6 and 7 and that over this very incident his brother PW 4 lodged First Information Report in the thana which was registered as CR case No. 106 of 1988 and she gave her statement to the Daroga in that case wherein she did not tell that the appellant raped her and in the salish also she did not tell that the appellant raped her and that in the night of the incident she and PWs 2 and 3 were sleeping on the same chowki and there was no other chowki in that room and she was sleeping on one side of the chowki and in the adjacent room PW 4 and his another brother Md Nurul Islam slept and his father slept in another room of the house and after hearing their alarm uncle Asgar and his wife and other members of the house adjacent to their house as well as neighbors Rabbani, Amiruddin, Mozammel, Tasir, Gadu and others came, and that the appellant is her cousin and that Asiruddin is her uncle. She denied the defence suggestion that there is a long standing dispute between the appellant and her father over land and the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case and that the thana did not take up her case as there was another GR Case over the same incident. The prosecutrix stated that she also did not hand over her wearing apparels to thana or to her lawyer. On recall, the PW 1 stated that after this case was filed, the Investigation Officer forcibly took the signature of PW 4 in some blank paper and after coming to know that she filed complaint to higher officials against the Investigation Officer but in cross-examination she stated that she has nothing to show that she filed complaint against the Investigation Officer. She further stated that first salish was held on 19-8-1988 and second salish was held on 22-8-1988 and she gave her statement to the Daroga twice.

4. PW 2 is the younger sister of the prosecutrix, she stated that three sisters were sleeping in the same room and two chowkies were place side by side in that room and the; prosecutrix slept in one chowki and she and PW 3 were sleeping in another chowki and she suddenly woke up on hearing some unusual sounds inside the room and at once she kindled a kupi lamp and found the appellant and the prosecutrix scuffling and then she stood by the side of door which was closed and then the appellant fled away through the gap between the wall and roof of the room and her sister caught hold of the leg of appellant to catch him but the appellant managed to escape. The prosecutrix later on told the persons present that the appellant has violated her and over this there was salish. She denied the suggestion of the defence that earlier she did not tell the Daroga about the incident of rape and also about the light of the kupi lamp, she also denied the suggestion of the defence that there was dispute with the appellant over the land so she deposed falsely against the appellant. PW 3, another sister of the prosecutrix, was tendered and in cross-examination she stated that all three sisters slept in the same chowki.

5. PW 4 is the brother of the prosecutrix. She stated that he slept in the room adjacent to the room of his sister and he woke hearing the hue and cry of his sisters and he instantly came out after opening his door and then the prosecutrix told him that the appellant entered into her room and now he has ascended on the roof. Thereafter he raised alarm and hearing the same uncle Asgar Ali neighbour Gobar Ali, Abdul Baki Moulavi, and other people came and he then asked the sisters to open the door and then they opened the door and the neighbors entered the room of her sisters and found the rope which was attached with the beam of the roof of the room. Then the prosecutrix told them that the appellant entered into her room secretly and got on the bed, lifted her clothes and then raped her. Then they went in search of the appellant but the appellants was not found at home, on the next day salish was held but the appellant did not attend the salish, then another salish was held in the Union Parishad office but the appellant did not also attend the said salish and hence, according to the advice of the persons present in those salish the prosecutrix filed the case in the Thana and since the Thana did not take up the case she then filed the complaint case. The court'' then passed order directing investigating and after about one month Daroga came for the investigation and asked them about the incident and seized the rope and also the papers regarding the salish and then after four months Daroga called him to the than and took his signature in written paper but without reading over to him the contents, subsequently he came to know that daroga Narayan Babu lodged the First Information Report showing him as informant and then he through the prosecutrix filed complaint against the said daroga and gave copy to different places. In cross-examination he denied the suggestion that he voluntarily lodged a written ejahar with the thana giving rise to the GR Case No. 106 of 1988 and now he is denying the same with ulterior motive. He stated that in the present case the daroga did not record his statement on 17-10-89 or on any subsequent date and the daroga also did not ask him any question. He denied the defence suggestion that he did not mention to Narayan Babu. Daroga about the incident of rape but stated that when he and other people went to the house of the appellant they were told that the appellant was at the godown where he was working as guard and he did not return to his house on that night, he stated that the incident occurred at about 10-00 PM and about 100 people assembled in the place of occurrence and he did not give any application to the Upazila Magistrate regarding the GR. Case and also did not give any copy of the complaint to him, and he did not know whether there was any case pending in Pirganj Thana against Babu and there are 3/4 cases against the father of Babu and that Babu was convicted. He stated that the house of PWs 5 and 6 is after interval 10/12 houses from their house and that of the PW 7 is situated at the last end of the village. He stated that in the salish Member Abdur Rashid and Dula Miah were present and put their signature in the salishnama but he did not have the salishnama and the members of the salish are not witnesses, in this case. He denied the defence suggestion that there was dispute between them and the appellant from the time of their father and so the appellant has been implicated falsely.

6. PW 5, who is not a charge sheet witness, stated that he at about 10-20 PM went to the house of the prosecutrix after hearing hue and cry and then the prosecutrix in presence of all stated that the appellant entered into her room and then he along with others went to the house of appellant but could not find him in this house and on the next day salish was held and the appellant was present in the salish and when the appellant was questioned he denied the allegation. He found marks of scratches on the chest and back of the appellant and when he questioned the appellant about the same the appellant left the salish and then and there salish was called in the local Union Parishad Office but the appellant did not attend that salish. In cross-examination he stated that after one month of the incident Narayan Babu went for investigation and asked him some questions and about 8-10 months after the incident Daroga Yusuf made investigation and asked questions. He denied the suggestion that he did not tell the Daroga in his 161 about statement, about his going to the place of occurrence after hearing the hue and cry and subsequent events like presence of other people at the place of occurrence and that the prosecutrix told them that the appellant raped her, hanging of the rope from the beam of the roofs, going to the house of appellant for apprehending him and holding of first salish and second salish, etc. PW 6, who is not a charge-sheeted witness, more or less corroborated the statement of PW 5.

7. PW 7 who is also not a charge sheet witness stated that his house is at interval of 5/6 houses from the house of the prosecutrix and after hearing the hue and cry he went to the house of the prosecutrix, told the persons present there that the appellant after entering into her room lifted her clothes and then raped her and then he along with others went in search of the appellant but did not find him at his house. On the next day there was a salish but the appellant did not turn up in the salish and thereafter another salish was held at the Union Parishad office but the appellant did not also turn up at the said salish. In cross-examination he stated that at first Daroga Narayan Babu examined him regarding the incident and after about two months Daroga Yusuf again examined him about the incident, He denied the defence suggestion that he did not tell the Yusuf Daroga during his examination under section 161 CrPC that the prosecutrix told him and as well as others that the appellant raped her and then he went to the house of the appellant to search him. He also denied the defence suggestion that the prosecutrix did not tell him anything about the incident.

8. PW 8 is the Advocate who prepared the petition of complaint which was filed by the prosecutrix on 25-8-1988 and he also proved the same which was marked as Exhibit I''. In cross-examination he stated that in the complaint petition there was no mention of discharging of semen in the private part of the prosecutrix and in the said petition PWs 4, 5 and 7 were not mentioned as witnesses.

9. PW 9 Md Yusuf Ali, Officer-in-Charge of Pirganj Thana, stated that on 17-10-1989 he received the petition of complaint through the court and then lodged the First Information Report and then proved the First Information Report and his signature. He stated that during investigation of the case he visited the place of occurrence and recorded the statement given under section 161 Cr PC and before 4/5 months of this investigation Daroga Narayan Babu made investigation over the self same incident and after investigation Daroga Narayan Babu filed the charge sheet against the appellant and the said investigation was started on the basis of the First Information Report lodged by PW 4 and after charge sheet was filed by Narayan Babu the court started further proceeding of the case will commence on the basis of the said charge sheet, the court directed him to investigate the case which was started on the basis of the First Information Report lodged by the prosecutrix and accordingly, he investigated the case. In cross-examination the PW 9 stated that the prosecutrix filed the complaint case in the court which was subsequently treated as First Information Report and that PWs 5, 6 and 7 are not charge sheet witnesses and that on 17-10-1989 he recorded the statements of PW 4 under section 161 CrPC. He further stated that PW 5 did not tell him that on the night of the incident prosecutrix in presence of all stated that the appellant entered into her room from the gap between the wall and the roof and gagged her mouth and then raped her and that he went to the house of the prosecutrix by hearing the hue and cry and that two salishes were held regarding the incident. He also stated that PW 6 also did not tell him that in the night of the incident the prosecutrix in presence of all stated that the appellant entered into her room and raped her and that after she shouted as কে কে the appellant identified himself as Chandu and that when the PWs 2 and 3 woke up after hearing the scuffle the appellant escaped by climbing the roof of the room. He also stated that PW 7 also did not state to him that the prosecutrix on the night of incident told him in presence of all that the appellant entered into her room and raped her. PW 9 further states that he also did not enquire whether the chairman and members were present in the salish. He further stated that after investigation he found that allegation under section 379 Penal Code has not been proved.

10. Narayan Chandra Datta, SI of Police was examined as DW 1 and he stated that on 1-12-1988 he was attached with Pirganj Police Station and GR Case No.106 of 1988 arose out of Pirganj PS Case No. 5 dated 31-12-1988 which was started out of the First Information Report lodged by PW 5 and the then Officer-in-Charge recorded the said First Information Report and this DW 1 proved the said First Information Report and the signature of the then Officer-in-Charge which was marked as Ext. Ka and Ka(I) and DW I stated that he knows the hand writing and the signature of the then Officer-in-Charge and the then Officer-in-Charge handed over the case to him for investigation, and PW 4, during investigation, admitted the he lodged the said First Information Report during investigation, the DW 1 also seized some alamats but did not seize the wearing apparels of the prosecutrix and the DW 1 also recorded the statement of some witnesses under section 161 Cr PC. The DW 1 also stated that in the aforesaid First Information Report which was lodged by PW 4 there is no mention of rape upon the prosecutrix and the prosecutrix in her statement given under section 161 Cr PC during the investigation of the said case did not state that the appellant raped her. DW 1 further stated that at first he did not know whether the prosecutrix filed the petition to the Magistrate court herself being the complainant but then subsequently came to know about the same and he did not enquire what happened to that said case. Mr Yusuf Ali, Officer-in-Charge investigated the Special Tribunal Case No.10 of 1990 which arose out of Purging PS Case No.3 dated 17-10-1988 in respect of the occurrence dated 18-8-1988. DW 1 also proved the order of stay which was passed by the Magistrate which was marked as Ext.3.

11. Mr Md Mansur Habib, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the conviction cannot be sustained because the entire case is concocted as will be evident from the inordinate delay in lodging the First Information Report and further, all the witnesses are relations of the prosecutrix and are interested witnesses. moreover, there are major contradictions in their depositions and that only the prosecutrix and PWs 2 to 4 are charge sheet witnesses, PWs 5, 6 and 7 are not charge sheet witnesses and PWs 8 and 9 are merely formal witnesses and further the prosecution without explanation at all with-held the other charge sheet witnesses. He referred to the evidence of prosecutrix and PW 2, the sister of the prosecutrix who slept with the prosecutrix in the same room at time of occurrence, and pointed to the contradiction regarding the manner of the alleged rape and also identification of the appellant and also about the manner and position of the chowki where the prosecutrix and her sisters were sleeping at the time of the commission of the alleged rape. Mr Habib further submits that in the present case the prosecutrix was not medically examined and her wearing apparels were also not sent for chemical examination and further though many witness came at the place of occurrence after hearing the hue and cry only the relations of the prosecutrix were examined and further the kupi lamp on the basis of which the prosecutrix and PW 2 recognised the appellants was also not seized. Mr Habib then submitted that this allegation of rape it concocted as will be evident from the fact that in the First Information Report it was stated that prosecutrix woke up when the appellant was raping her but during examination-in-chief and also cross-examination she stated that she woke up when the appellant tried to rape her and further, as it will appear from the deposition of PW 9 and DW 1 that for the self same incident which occurred on 18-8-1988 PW 4 lodged a First Information Report out of which GR Case No. 106 of 1988 arose wherein during investigation PWs 4 and the prosecutrix were also examined but in their statement made under section 161 CrPC there was no allegation of rape. Mr Habib further submits that admittedly the father of the prosecutrix was in the same house at the night of the incident and as per the prosecutrix case after hearing the hue and cry of the prosecutrix and PWs 2-4 Asiruddin, other neighbours came out but surprisingly the father of the prosecutrix Asimuddin and other neighbours were not examined in the case and the chairman or Members of the Union Parishad, who, according to the prosecutrix, conducted the salish, were also not examined. Mr. Habib also referred to the statement of PW 9 in cross-examination where he stated that these PWs 5, 6 and 7 did not tell him that after they went to the place of occurrence, the prosecutrix told the persons assembled therein that the appellant entered into her room and raped her.

12. Mr Syed Abu Kawser, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the State, submits that the evidence of the prosecutrix who is the victim and injured person should be believed and that when appellant did not attend the first salish as well as the second salish held in the Union Parishad Office the prosecutrix lodged the petition of complaint which was subsequently treated as First Information Report and so the delay has been explained, further the discrepancy in the evidence of the witnesses of the prosecutrix are minor which prove that the witnesses are natural witnesses and they are not tutored.

13. Heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the evidence on records. It appears that among the witnesses only the prosecutrix and PW 2 are eye witnesses as PW 3 has been tendered. The First Information Report case is that the prosecutrix woke up when the appellant was raping her after undressing her and when she shouted as কে কে the appellant asked her to remain silent after disclosing his identity as Chandu and then gagged her mouth with his hand, at that time at the sound of the scuffle PWs 2 and 3 woke up and started shouting and then PW 2 took up a match from below of pillow igniting the match and kindled the kupi lamp and with the light of the kupi lamp she saw the appellant and the prosecutrix scuffling and the PW 2 when appellant was fleeing away wanted to resist the appellant by dragging his leg but she did not succeed. However during her deposition the prosecutrix stated that she woke up when in the night someone tried to rape her and then she shouted as কে, কে, but the appellant gagged her mouth and she then tried to resist the appellant and hearing the sound of the scuffle PW 2 lighted kupi lamp and she then found that the appellant did this act. So it appears that there is clear contradiction regarding the manner of committing rape and regarding identification of the accused and in the facts and circumstances of the present case these contradictions cannot be termed as minor discrepancy as in the First Information Report the prosecutrix stated that she woke up while being raped but in the examination-in-chief at First Information Report she stated that she woke up when the appellant tried to rape her but later stated that the appellant discharged semen inside her private part. Further, PW 2 in her deposition stated that after hearing the sound of scuffle she lighted the kupi lamp with a match and found that the appellant Chandu and the prosecutrix were in the midst of scuffle and then the appellant tried to escape by climbing to the roof but her sister tried to resist him by grabbing his leg but the prosecutrix in her deposition stated the PW 2 grabbed his leg while he was escaping and in the First Information Report the prosecutrix stated that PW 2 grabbed the leg of the appellant. This is a major contradiction Moreover. PW 1 during her cross-examination, stated that in her room there was pne chowki and all the sisters were sleeping on the said chowki and there was no other chowki in the said room but PW 2 during her examination in chief stated there are 2 chowkies in the said room which was placed side by side and the informant slept in one chowki and she and PW 3 slept in one other chowki and PW 3 who was tendered in her cross-examination stated that all the three sisters slept in the same chowki so that is also major contradiction regarding the manner in which the PWs 1, 2, and 3 were sleeping in the room on the night of the occurrence. Further, from the evidence of PW 9 the Investigation Officer and DW 1 it appears that over this self same incident which occurred in the night of 18-8-1988 another case was also lodged and during the investigation of said case the prosecutrix as well as the PW 4 gave statement to the investigation officer of that case under section 161 Cr PC wherein they did not disclose the incident of rape as has been alleged in the present case though it arose out of the self same incident.

<u>14. It is true that ordinarily in case of rape the evidence of the prosecutrix who is the injured person is believed but in the present case the contradictions are so major that the evidence of the prosecutrix cannot be believed more so when PW 2, an eye-witness according to prosecutrix, did not prove rape and PW 3 who according to prosecution is another eye-witness slept in the same chowki with the prosecutrix was only tendered. Further, the prosecution withheld the witnesses named in the charge sheet without giving any explanation for their withholding and introduced PWs 5, 6 and 7 who are not charge sheet witnesses. Further in the present case the prosecutrix was also not medically examined and the prosecution also did not taking any steps for chemical examination of the wearing apparels of the prosecutrix which is a vital omission on the part of the prosecution.</u>

15. It thus appears that the prosecution failed to prove their case beyond doubt and accordingly, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence cannot be sustained and is liable to be set aside.

In the result, the appeal is allowed and the impugned Judgment and order dated 5-5-90 convicting and sentencing the appellants is hereby set aside and the appellant is acquitted of the charge in the aforesaid case and be released from the bail bond.

End.
